messages:
ben: Thinking out loudwe're proposing a "local KMS proxy" sidecar for Private deployments to forward calls to customer HSMs. Main ask: how do we prove to auditors that we never store or leak key material or direct key ids?

olivia: Requirements I care about: (1) one-way key identifier (no reversible ID), (2) canonical audit schema that ties to customer HSM logs via trace IDs, (3) RBAC that forbids any export/unwrap operations, (4) clear retention/eraser controls.

sara: Practicals: fingerprinting with sha256(key_id || salt) where salt is per-customer and rotated only by customer. We store only fingerprint. Any redaction we do must be deterministic so auditor can map events if customer shares salt, but we never store the salt.

ben: Example audit line (single-line JSON for logs): {"ts":"2026-03-05T09:23:11Z","actor":"svc:invoice-ingest","op":"Decrypt","key_fp":"sha256:ab12...","trace":"rwd:xyz789","result":"ok","proxy_ver":"1.2.0"}

sec-bot: Note: scrub headers matching /x-?key|key-?id/i and env var patterns KEY_* in startup logs. Add runtime redact config for custom vendor headers.

lin: Security constraints: run sidecar as unprivileged user, drop CAP_SYS_PTRACE, use seccomp to limit syscalls, and use namespace isolation. Also use mTLS to the customer's HSM endpoint; require client certs pinned to customer cert thumbprint.

olivia: RBAC sketch: two roles: kms-proxy-invoker (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign) and kms-proxy-maintainer (RotateAliases, Disable). Explicit deny for ExportKey and GetKeyMaterial. Also restrict policies to resources matching hashed fingerprints only.

sara: Incident playbook (short): 1) detect anomalous pattern (rate/shape) 2) cordon proxy instances for affected tenant, 3) collect our proxy logs (hashed fp + traces) and ask customer for HSM audit extract (timestamp range + HSM event ids), 4) if compromise plausible, instruct customer on rotating wrapping keys and non-exportable keys, 5) produce a signed incident timeline and chain of custody bundle for SOC2 evidence.

ben: Ops asks: retention default 365d for enterprise (configurable), endpoint to export logs filtered by trace id, and SLA to deliver zipped evidence within 72h for legal/compliance requests.

lin: On third-party libs: we use a PKCS#11 adapter in the shim. If a CVE shows up we need: 1) inventory mapping to sidecar builds, 2) emergency backport/patch plan, 3) compensating controls (WAF/rate-limit, sandboxing), 4) customer notification template. Prefer vendor attestation APIs rather than parsing PKCS#11 outputs when possible.

olivia: Testing checklist: unit tests for deterministic hashing, redaction tests (assert no raw key-id appears), integration test with a fake HSM that asserts no key material flows through our process, load test to keep sidecar p95 added latency <10ms.

sara: Compliance note: for PCI we may need an additional attestation that our logs are immutable for the retention period (WORM). Consider adding a write-once log sink or signed append-only log that customers can verify.

ben: Action items: olivia -> draft IAM JSON and example least-privilege policy; lin -> harden container seccomp profile + cert pinning; sara -> incident evidence template and retention config; sec-bot -> add automated redaction check to CI. I'll assemble a short FAQ for customers explaining fingerprints, why we don't keep salts, and how to request trace exports.

sec-bot: CI tasks queued: redact unit test, fingerprint reversibility test, load gate.

ben: Great, let's move this into the security sprint board. Thanks everyone. :+1:
